question: Given the GEFSv12 control-member rain forecast for the local days t+1, t+2 and t+3 (basin means, bias-corrected on the validation years, from the 00 UTC run of the UTC date t+1, the latest run that exists at the issue time) as three extra daily inputs beside the AORC rain to midnight, how many more onsets are warned 1, 2 and 3 days ahead - when the network was trained on the AORC rain of those days (an analysis made after the fact) and run on the forecast (E2a, main split), and when it is retrained with the forecast as an input (E2b, satellite-era split) - against the same network without the forecast, against a shuffled forecast with the right climate and no information about the day, and against a perfect rain forecast?
outcome: Given the GEFS control-member rain forecast for the next three days (bias-corrected) as an input beside the rain to midnight, onsets warned 1/2/3 days ahead at the fixed warning level go from 51%/21%/12% to 45%/39%/37% (at the level chosen on the validation years: 51%/33%/21% to 54%/58%/51%; the shuffled-forecast control, 14%/4%/4%, is not a neutral baseline - it measures the harm of misleading slots to a network that trusts them - and the clean control, E2b's, equals the model without the forecast); median NSE from 0.77/0.38/0.25 to 0.69/0.53/0.45 (control 0.60/0.19/0.03), 'mixed' by the rule of report section 4.2 at all three leads; the verdict is NOT YET.
outcome_caveat: At the fixed warning level (trigger 1.0, the level of every score of the ladder) the forecast adds -6.7, +18.2 and +25.3 points of onsets warned at 1, 2 and 3 days ahead against lstm_wqa (reading of the onsets by the seed rule, every single training of one above every single training of the other: clear loss, clear gain and clear gain) and -0.074, +0.155 and +0.201 of median NSE (reading of the NSE by the rule of report section 4.2: mixed, mixed and mixed); at the level chosen on the validation years the differences in onsets warned are +2.6, +25.3 and +29.7 points; at equal false-warning budgets (test years, any level; at most 40% of the onset warnings false) +9.3, +27.3 and +23.3 points and (at most 50% false) +11.3, +40.0 and +42.1; and the trigger-free average precision of the onset warnings goes from 0.462/0.236/0.176 to 0.527/0.471/0.448 (differences with 95% block-bootstrap intervals: 1 day: +0.065 (+0.006 to +0.126); 2 days: +0.235 (+0.162 to +0.300); 3 days: +0.272 (+0.203 to +0.335)). The 1-day difference at the fixed level (-6.7 points) is a moved operating point and is not established as a loss of skill: the forecast model's warnings are fewer and more often right (false warnings among the onset warnings 35% against 50%; CSI 0.358 against 0.337); at the level chosen on the validation years (trigger 0.90 against 1.00) it warns of 54% against 51% of the onsets (+2.6 points; false warnings 44% against 50%; CSI 0.379 against 0.337); a block bootstrap over the test days (30-day blocks) puts the fixed-level difference at -6.7 points (-14.2 to -0.1), which is borderline, and the paired sign test over onsets counts onsets as independent, which they are not (onsets cluster in storms and across basins). That the substitution networks over-trust slots that were exact in training is a hypothesis, not a finding. For it: the same networks warn of 69% of the 1-day onsets given the perfect rain, 45% given the forecast and 14% given a shuffled forecast (51% with no slots), and the networks retrained with the forecast (E2b) gain +20.3 points at 1 day with a harmless control. Against it, or not separating it from other causes: of the 127 onsets that lstm_wqa warns and the forecast model misses, 46 (36%) are missed even when the slots hold the perfect rain; the difference at the fixed level sits in onsets with little rain on the target day (220 of 611 with under 5 mm: 80% warned without the forecast, 42% with it, 62% with the perfect rain in the slots), follows the seasons (points of onsets warned, forecast model minus lstm_wqa: DJF +4.1, MAM -10.6, JJA -21.5, SON -8.9) and is found in 8 of 12 basins; and the forecast is light where the onsets are (it carries 0.69 of the AORC rain on the onset days and 0.63 on those with at least 5 mm, a conditional bias that the single bias factor does not remove) and has 36% exact zeros against 51% in the AORC rain. No experiment here isolates the cause: the alternatives are the warning level, small-rain onsets and a conditional bias of the forecast. Forward passes of the saved networks (forward_pass_tests; information only, nothing retrained): slots = (1 - w) x the perfect rain + w x the forecast, onsets warned at 1 day for w = 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1: 69.1%, 64.6%, 58.6%, 51.2%, 44.5%; the first quarter of the way from the perfect rain to the forecast costs 18%/19%/19% of the drop in onsets warned at 1/2/3 days (a linear response would cost 25%), so the response is gradual, not steep at small departures from exact slots, which a reliance on exactness would predict; the forecast values below 0.5 mm set to zero: 44.2%, below 1 mm: 43.9% (at most 0.7 points of difference from the forecast at any lead). The shuffled-forecast control of E2a is not a neutral baseline: the network was trained on exact slots and collapses when the slots hold noise (14%/4%/4% against 51%/21%/12% with no slots; median NSE 0.60/0.19/0.03 against 0.77/0.38/0.25), so the comparison with it measures the harm of misleading slots to a network that trusts them, not the information of the forecast: the forecast is +30.1, +34.9 and +32.7 points above it, which says little, and the second half of the success rule (above the control) is met by a wide margin at every lead. The information test is E2b's control, trained and run on shuffled slots: it equals the model without slots (41%/15%/8% against 41%/14%/8%), and the forecast is +20.6, +34.3 and +36.0 points above it. Of the gap in onsets warned between lstm_wqa and a perfect rain forecast of the three days (lstm_wqaP warns of 66%/69%/71%) the forecast closes -45%, 37% and 42% at 1, 2 and 3 days ahead at the fixed level, and -256%, 38% and 39% of the NSE gap (a negative share: the forecast model is below lstm_wqa); against the old perfect-weather upper bound (lstm_wqf: 64%/67%/68%) it closes -51%, 39% and 44% of the onset gap beyond lstm_wqa. Retrained with the forecast as an input on the shorter satellite-era split (train 2000-2008, 4 test years with 335/540/656 onsets at 1/2/3 days ahead; its own scores, NOT comparable with the main split; its base is weaker: lstm_wqa_s warns of 41%/14%/8% against 51%/21%/12% for lstm_wqa), onsets warned go from 41%/14%/8% (no forecast) to 61%/49%/44% at the fixed level (control 41%/15%/8%, equal to the model without the forecast; perfect rain 72%/77%/77%), +20.3, +35.2 and +36.4 points, against -6.7, +18.2 and +25.3 for the substitution on the main split - the contrast mixes two splits and two bases and is not a measurement. At the level chosen on the validation years the E2b differences are +23.6, +19.8 and +12.5 points (the validation-chosen trigger of lstm_wqa_s, the model without the forecast, is 1.05/0.75/0.65 at 1/2/3 days, at 51%/77%/82% false warnings: where it is below 1 it buys onsets with false warnings, so the fixed level flatters the gain of the forecast there); the CSI differences are +0.127, +0.239 and +0.257 at the fixed level and +0.127, +0.202 and +0.196 at the chosen level; the trigger-free average precision gains +0.184, +0.300 and +0.321. The bias factors were fitted on 2000-2005, inside its training years (scalars; nothing of its validation or test years). On the plain gauge model, without the rain to midnight, the same forecast takes onsets warned from 19%/8%/6% to 31%/36%/36% (+12.8, +28.0 and +30.3 points). Ridge regression and the random forest given the same inputs (the forecast substituted in the same way) warn of 69%/59%/52% and 55%/47%/42% of the onsets at 1/2/3 days ahead at the fixed level, with a median NSE of 0.71/0.41/0.36 and 0.72/0.54/0.47 (the LSTM: 45%/39%/37%, 0.69/0.53/0.45; the forecast adds +13.6/+38.7/+39.9 and +6.9/+25.0/+29.9 points of onsets to them, -6.7/+18.2/+25.3 to the LSTM; false warnings among the onset warnings: ridge 62%/60%/61%, forest 45%/47%/49%, LSTM 35%/40%/41%: they warn of more onsets with more false warnings, a different operating point). Without a trigger (average precision of the onset warnings at 1/2/3 days: ridge 0.438/0.414/0.391, forest 0.500/0.460/0.420, LSTM 0.527/0.471/0.448) the forest minus the LSTM is -0.027, -0.011, -0.028 (intervals include 0: level with the LSTM) and ridge minus the LSTM -0.089, -0.057, -0.056 (intervals exclude 0: below the LSTM); at 1 day ahead, by the paired reading of the onsets at the fixed level: ridge, the simple model warns of more onsets; forest, the simple model warns of more onsets; by the NSE (report section 4.2): against ridge, no clear difference; against the forest, no clear difference - the gain of the forecast, in onsets and in NSE at every lead, does not need the network. Caveats that are part of the result: control member only (no ensemble); 0.25 degree boxes over basins of 113 to 1,928 km2; the bias factor (one per basin and lead, median 0.99) was fitted on the validation years 2000-2005, is noisy (fitted on the two halves of those years the factors differ by a median 10%/12%/14% at 1/2/3 days) and leaves a seasonal bias (mean ratio forecast / AORC at 1 day: 1.12 in summer, 0.88 in winter) and a conditional one (the corrected forecast carries 0.71/0.66/0.62 of the AORC rain on days with at least 5 mm at 1/2/3 days); raw and corrected forecasts give nearly the same onsets (+0.0, -0.5 and +0.2 points, corrected minus raw), so the correction is not what carries the result; the substitution networks never saw a forecast in training; the rain to midnight of the base rung is the AORC analysis, made after the fact (corrections about 10 days after the hour; hours before 2002 are disaggregated daily totals), not rain that could be read at midnight - the independent review of E1b tested the hindsight risk on 78 test-year days (coefficient of the pre-midnight AORC rain on the later Stage IV rain about -0.03, 95% interval -0.06 to -0.001: nothing positive) and found that with Stage IV, a real-time product, in its place for the issue day the same networks warned of 86 to 95 of the 171 onsets of those days against 92 with AORC; the other 440 of the 611 onsets were not tested (numbers as the review's verdict states them: results/review_aorc_rain_to_midnight.json); in Eastern summer the last files of the run (from forecast hour 39 on) are posted up to 15 minutes after the issue time (results/gefs_basins.json, realtime_margin), and that margin rests on the posting times of the OPERATIONAL control member on 4 days of October 2026 (results/data_access.json), not on a long record and not on the reforecast archive, which is not an operational archive (its skill is an estimate of the operational skill, to be checked on a few months of operational GEFS before any real-time claim); three trainings per set, so the single-training ranges are the only repetition (five would settle the 'mixed' readings of the NSE at 2 and 3 days).

e2_success.rule: NEXT_STEPS_FOR_AGENTS.md, E2: a clear gain in onsets warned at 2 and 3 days ahead, where the room is largest. Read here as: at that lead every single training of lstm_wqaF_sub warns of more onsets than every single training of lstm_wqa (no forecast) AND than every single training of the control lstm_wqaF_clim (the criterion of report section 4.2 for onsets: the seeds are the only repetition the pooled onsets have)
e2_success.second_half_of_the_rule_says_little: the margin over the E2a control is +30/+35/+33 points at 1/2/3 days: the control measures the harm of misleading slots to a network that trusts them, not the information of the forecast, so 'above the control' is met by a wide margin whatever the forecast is worth; the first half (above lstm_wqa) carries the rule

inputs.how_to_read: the hours each input covers, as the model reads them on issue day t. The forecast is issued at the end of day t, local midnight of the river-flow day

clock.input: prcp (Daymet rain, the rain table), srad, tmax, tmin, vp, dayl
clock.covers: for rain, a day that ends at about 09:00 local standard time on day t (results/day_windows.json, day_ends.daymet); the window of the other Daymet variables was not measured

clock.used_by: every set (all with the river gauge)
clock.covers: the daily mean flow of local day t, midnight to midnight by the local clock, so the day ends at the issue time

clock.used_by: every set except wqF_sub and wq_s
clock.covers: the AORC rain of the wall-clock day t, 00:00 to 24:00 (summer time included): the hours up to the issue time; AORC is an analysis made after the fact
clock.source: data/aorc, summed by gefs_to_basins.aorc_local_days (the code of 16_aorc_rain_to_midnight.py)

clock.covers: the AORC rain of the local days t+1, t+2, t+3: rain that has not fallen at the issue time (a perfect forecast, an upper bound that cannot be had in practice)

fs1..fs3: the AORC rain of the local days t+1..t+3 (p) for the issue days up to 2000-09-30, the bias-corrected GEFS control-member forecast of the same days from 2000-10-01 (validation and test years)

fk1..fk3: p for the issue days up to 2000-09-30; from 2000-10-01 the bias-corrected forecast shuffled within (basin, calendar month) across years, the three leads of a day together (no information about the day)

clock.used_by: wqaF_sub_raw (with --raw); the raw forecast is also given to the saved wqaF_sub networks at prediction time
clock.covers: fr1..fr3: p up to 2000-09-30; from 2000-10-01 the RAW (not bias-corrected) GEFS forecast
fc1..fc3: the bias-corrected GEFS control-member forecast of the local days t+1..t+3, in every year of the table (2000-01-01 on)
fx1..fx3: the bias-corrected forecast shuffled within (basin, calendar month) across years, the three leads together, in every year of the table (the control)
fixed numbers per basin, not daily data

rule.run: the 00 UTC run of the UTC date t+1 (init_date = t+1): 4 h old at the Eastern issue time in summer, 5 h in winter, 5 or 6 h at the Central one (the latest 00 UTC run that exists at the issue time; the run of the date t+2 starts after it)
rule.local_day: local day t+k = the wall-clock day of the gauge (zoneinfo America/New_York, America/Chicago for Leaf River, summer time included), forecast hours (lo, hi] of the run with lo = local midnight that starts the day, hi = the one that ends it, counted from the run's start; the amounts of the 3-hourly windows inside the day are summed, a window that straddles a boundary is split in proportion to the time inside (1/3 or 2/3, uniform rain inside a window assumed)
rule.basin_mean: sum over the grid boxes of weight x rain, the weights being the shares of the outline's area in each 0.25 degree box (exact intersections in EPSG:5070)
rule.tables: the first row is 2000-01-01; k = 1, 2, 3 in the column names; mm per local day; fc_raw = the forecast as the model gives it, fc_bc = fc_raw x the bias factor of the basin and lead, aorc = the AORC rain of the same local day t+k

bias.rule: bias factor per basin and lead = (sum of the AORC rain of the local days t+k) / (sum of the forecast rain of the same days) over the issue days whose TARGET day t+k lies in the validation years 2000-10-01 .. 2005-09-30 (flood.SPLIT['val']); fc_bc = fc_raw x factor, for every day of 2000-2014 (a factor fitted on the validation years only, applied unchanged to the test years); a single factor per basin and lead: no seasonal correction

asserted: run init (00 UTC of the UTC date t+1) <= issue time (local midnight at the end of day t)
run init + 24 h > issue time (no fresher 00 UTC run exists)
every forecast hour of days t+1..t+3 is after the issue time (hour > 0 of the run) and inside the day's UTC span
day t+1 starts exactly at the issue time, day t+k+1 starts where day t+k ends
no forecast hour beyond 78 (the last stored window)
days have 23, 24 or 25 hours, and the window weights of a day add up to hours / 3
the weights from forecast hours equal the weights from absolute (epoch-second) times
run init (00 UTC of the UTC date t+1) <= issue time (local midnight at the end of day t)
run init + 24 h > issue time (no fresher 00 UTC run exists)
every forecast hour of days t+1..t+3 is after the issue time (hour > 0 of the run) and inside the day's UTC span
day t+1 starts exactly at the issue time, day t+k+1 starts where day t+k ends
no forecast hour beyond 78 (the last stored window)
days have 23, 24 or 25 hours, and the window weights of a day add up to hours / 3
the weights from forecast hours equal the weights from absolute (epoch-second) times

caveats: Control member only (c00, 'low-res ctl'): no ensemble mean, no spread. A single deterministic member is noisier than the 5-member mean and its day totals place the rain to within the forecast's own timing error.

The grid boxes are 0.25 degree (about 25 km, 630 km2) and the basins 113 to 1,928 km2: 1 to 9 boxes overlap a basin (weights recorded in basins.<id>.weights). The forecast is the model's box-mean rain, smoother and drier in its peaks than a basin mean of 1 km rain.

The issue-time margin (realtime_margin): a real-time service would have the run 40 to 100 minutes before the issue time in winter and about 15 minutes too late for the last files (hours after about 39) in Eastern summer; this archive does not check whether the operational control member had the same posting times in 2000-2014, and the 00 UTC run was the only one of the reforecast. The rule 'the run of the UTC date t+1' is kept for every day and basin, as the work order says.

The bias factor is one number per basin and lead fitted on the validation years (mean AORC / mean forecast). The forecast's bias has a season (by_season in the skill record: a wetter control member in spring and summer), which one factor does not remove; a seasonal factor was not used.
AORC is the reference, not the truth: an analysis anchored on gauges and radar (hours before 2002 disaggregated daily totals). The forecast's skill 'against AORC' is skill against that analysis.

Rain amounts of a local day are the sum of 3-hourly windows with straddling windows split in proportion (uniform rain inside a window assumed); for a=4, 5 or 6 the first window of day t+1 is split 1/3-2/3 or 2/3-1/3 or not at all, and the same at the end of each day.
The Brier scores belong to a deterministic forecast (yes/no) or to a calibration of its amount; neither is the probability forecast of an ensemble.

value_of_the_forecast.what: THE POINT OF E2. lstm_wqaF_sub minus lstm_wqa: the worth of the bias-corrected GEFS control-member rain forecast of the local days t+1..t+3 as three extra daily inputs beside the AORC rain to midnight, with the river gauge, on the main split (test years 2005-2014). wqaF_sub was trained on the AORC rain of those days (an analysis made after the fact; it never saw a forecast in training), stopped on the validation years with the real forecast in the slots and scored on the test years with it; wqa is the same network without the three columns (script 16). The two have different numbers of inputs, so the same seed number gives different starting weights. The numbers of by_lead are at the FIXED warning level (trigger 1.0) and the readings of the seed rule are about that level: at 1 day it moves the operating point (fewer, more often right warnings), so read operating_points beside it: the same comparison at the level chosen on the validation years, at equal false-warning budgets, without a trigger (average precision) and with block-bootstrap intervals. Quote it with its companions (forecast_vs_climatology_control and retrained_vs_substituted): the forecast's value is read against the control with the same climate and no information about the day.

forecast_vs_climatology_control.what: lstm_wqaF_sub minus lstm_wqaF_clim: the forecast against a forecast with the right climate and no information about the day (the same forecasts shuffled within basin and calendar month across years, the three leads of a day together). The control was trained, stopped and scored exactly like wqaF_sub. THIS CONTROL IS NOT A NEUTRAL BASELINE: the E2a networks were trained on exact slots, so given slots with no information they collapse far below lstm_wqa (see value_of_a_misleading_input): the difference measures the harm of misleading slots to a network that trusts them, not the information of the forecast, and it is large at every lead whatever the forecast is worth. The clean information test is E2b's control (retrained_vs_substituted.retrained_against_its_control), trained and run on shuffled slots, which equals the model without slots.

retrained_vs_substituted.what: E2b against E2a. retrained = lstm_wqaF_s minus lstm_wqa_s, both retrained on the satellite-era split (train 2000-10-01..2008-09-30, validation 2008-10-01..2010-09-30, test 2010-10-01..2014-09-30), so the network learns the forecast's own errors; substituted = lstm_wqaF_sub minus lstm_wqa on the main split (test 2005-2014), set beside it. THE TWO ARE NOT COMPARABLE IN LEVEL: the E2b split trains on 8 years instead of 20, its test years are 2010-2014 (4 years, other onsets, other flood thresholds from its own training years; the E2b base lstm_wqa_s is weaker than lstm_wqa), so compare the gains, not the scores, and read a difference between the two gains as a hint, not as a measurement: it mixes two splits and two bases. The E2b control (retrained_against_its_control), trained and run on shuffled slots, equals the model without slots and is the clean information test; retrained_operating_points gives the E2b comparison at the level chosen on the validation years, at equal false-warning budgets and without a trigger.

notes: Quoting. The sentence in `outcome` is accurate arithmetic but incomplete as a statement of the result: any document (report, README, slides, Q&A, guide) must quote `outcome_full` (the outcome plus `outcome_caveat`), never `outcome` alone. Both are computed from the tables of this file. The numbers of E2b (the satellite-era split) are comparable only with each other.

Clock of the forecast columns. Every forecast column is dated by the ISSUE day t: the value on row t is the forecast rain of the local wall-clock day t+k (k = 1, 2, 3; zoneinfo America/New_York, America/Chicago for Leaf River, summer time included, the same day convention as the AORC input of script 16) from the 00 UTC run of the UTC date t+1, the latest run that exists at the issue time (local midnight at the end of day t: 04, 05 or 06 UTC of that date; the run is 4 to 6 hours old). code/gefs_to_basins.py asserts for all 5387 issue days and both time zones that the run starts at or before the issue time, that no fresher 00 UTC run exists, that every forecast hour of the three days lies after the issue time and inside the day's UTC span, that the three days follow each other hour by hour and that no hour beyond 78 is read; it computes the window weights by a second route (absolute times) and replaces all later runs by random rain (no forecast issued earlier changes); and it checks the hours of the two products against each other (results/gefs_basins.json, clock). The engine reads the dyn columns of the days up to and including the issue day; the made-up-values test of this file (causality) replaces the forecast columns (and, in a second round, every input column and the flow) after a cut day by random values on the saved networks: no forecast issued on or before the cut day changes, the later ones do. flood.fit also ran flood._assert_causal on every network.

The substitution design (E2a). The slot columns hold, for the issue days up to 2000-09-30 (the training years; 7305 days), the AORC rain of the local days t+1..t+3 (an analysis made after the fact: a perfect forecast), and from 2000-10-01 (validation and test years; 5113 days) the bias-corrected GEFS forecast of the same days. The networks are trained on the first part only (the trainer samples sequences that end inside the training years and scores the loss on training target days), so they never see a forecast in training; the trainer scores the validation years from the same table, so its stopping point is chosen with the real forecast in the slots; the test years are scored with it. The split is by the ISSUE day of the slots, so the forecasts for the first validation target days (2000-10-01 .. 2000-10-03: 1 forecast at lead 1, 2 at lead 2, 3 at lead 3 per basin, 6 of about 5,500) are issued on days whose slots still hold the AORC rain; the test years are not affected. The GEFS forecast of 2000-01-01 .. 2000-09-30 exists and is not used in E2a (those days are training years). The forecast columns of E2b hold the forecast in every year of its table (2000-01-01 on).

The control. fk (E2a) and fx (E2b) hold the same forecasts in another order: within each basin and calendar month the rows (the three leads of one day together) are permuted so that no day keeps a forecast of its own calendar year (fixed seeds; asserted: the sorted values of every calendar month are the same as the forecast's, no day keeps its year). The median correlation of the control columns with the AORC rain of the day is 0.004 (E2a; range -0.019 to 0.083 over basins and leads), that of the forecast 0.654: the control has the right climate of each calendar month (hence a small positive correlation through the seasonal cycle) and no information about the day. It is NOT a neutral baseline for E2a: the E2a networks were trained on exact slots, so given such a control they collapse (14%/4%/4% of the onsets against 51%/21%/12% with no slots, median NSE 0.60/0.19/0.03 against 0.77/0.38/0.25); the comparison with it measures the harm of misleading slots to a network that trusts them, not the information of the forecast. The information test is E2b's control, trained and run on shuffled slots, which equals the model without slots (41%/15%/8% against 41%/14%/8%).

The forecast's own skill (results/gefs_basins.json; raw control-member forecast against the AORC rain of the same local days, all days 2000-2014, median over the 12 basins), 1/2/3 days ahead: correlation 0.72/0.66/0.59, mean ratio forecast / AORC 0.98/0.96/0.94; by season (lead 1) the correlation is DJF 0.81, MAM 0.74, JJA 0.51, SON 0.78 and the mean ratio DJF 0.88, MAM 1.02, JJA 1.12, SON 0.97. Brier skill of days with at least 5 mm (test years; yes/no forecast of the control member / a calibrated probability fitted on the validation years): 0.16/0.07/-0.05 / 0.44/0.39/0.33; at least 10 mm: 0.05/0.00/-0.11 / 0.37/0.32/0.26. The lag check holds (best shift 0 in every basin and lead: True; median correlation at lead 1 0.72 at shift 0 against 0.17 and 0.15 one day earlier and later).

Bias correction. One factor per basin and lead = mean AORC rain / mean forecast rain over the validation years (target days 2000-10-01 .. 2005-09-30), applied unchanged to every day of 2000-2014, test years included (a factor from earlier years): median over the basins 0.99/1.01/1.02, range over the basins 0.89 to 1.38/0.85 to 1.40/0.87 to 1.41 (the two Florida basins need 1.2 to 1.4: the forecast is drier than AORC there; a cause was not looked for). It is a single factor, so the seasonal bias (mean ratio by season, lead 1, validation years: DJF 0.95, MAM 1.05, JJA 1.07, SON 0.93) is not removed. In E2b the factor was fitted on 2000-2005, which lies inside that split's training years (a scalar fitted with the training-year rain; nothing of its validation or test years). The raw forecast is scored too: readings.raw_vs_bias_corrected.

0.25 degree boxes over small basins. The model's grid boxes are about 630 km2; the 12 outlines (113 to 1,928 km2) overlap 1 to 9 boxes each (the weights are the exact area shares in an equal-area projection, recorded in results/gefs_basins.json, basins, and checked against a fine raster to within 0.007); the forecast is the box-mean rain of a model with 0.25 degree physics, smoother than a basin mean of 1 km rain, and the correlation with AORC is lower in summer convection (JJA, lead 1: 0.51).

Control member only. Only the control member (c00) of the GEFSv12 reforecast was fetched; the archive holds more members (ROADMAP.md: 5 members; data/gefs/README.md: more on Wednesdays), their mean and their spread were not used. A single member is a sharper and noisier forecast than the ensemble mean; the ensemble would give a smoother amount and, with its spread, a probability, neither of which is tried here. The Brier skills above are those of one member (yes/no, or calibrated), not of an ensemble, and are not a check of the ensemble numbers of Guan et al. (2022).

The issue-time margin. The 00 UTC run is the latest run that exists at the issue time, but a real-time service would have its files only after the model has run: the operational control member posts its forecast-hour-78 file about 4.26 hours after the run's start (results/data_access.json; 4 days sampled in October 2026: a short record of the OPERATIONAL system, not the reforecast archive, which has no posting times and is not an operational archive; the skill of the reforecast is an estimate of the operational skill). Margin of the last needed file at the issue time: Eastern winter (run 5 h old) 45 minutes, Eastern summer (run 4 h old) -15 minutes (the 14 files from hour 39 on are posted up to 15 minutes after it), Central 45 and 105 minutes. The rule 'the run of the UTC date t+1' is kept for every day and basin (the work order's rule), so the experiment is slightly optimistic in Eastern summer; issuing at 00:30 local would restore the margin.

E2b is a different experiment on a different split (train 2000-10-01..2008-09-30, validation 2008-10-01..2010-09-30, test 2010-10-01..2014-09-30; flood thresholds from its own training years): 8 years of training instead of 20, 4 test years instead of 9, other onsets (see the number of onsets in the readings). The 1-day result of E2a, read with its evidence (a reading of the numbers in this file; the review of E2 asked for it). The 1-day difference at the fixed level (-6.7 points) is a moved operating point and is not established as a loss of skill: the forecast model's warnings are fewer and more often right (false warnings among the onset warnings 35% against 50%; CSI 0.358 against 0.337); at the level chosen on the validation years (trigger 0.90 against 1.00) it warns of 54% against 51% of the onsets (+2.6 points; false warnings 44% against 50%; CSI 0.379 against 0.337); a block bootstrap over the test days (30-day blocks) puts the fixed-level difference at -6.7 points (-14.2 to -0.1), which is borderline, and the paired sign test over onsets counts onsets as independent, which they are not (onsets cluster in storms and across basins). That the substitution networks over-trust slots that were exact in training is a hypothesis, not a finding. For it: the same networks warn of 69% of the 1-day onsets given the perfect rain, 45% given the forecast and 14% given a shuffled forecast (51% with no slots), and the networks retrained with the forecast (E2b) gain +20.3 points at 1 day with a harmless control. Against it, or not separating it from other causes: of the 127 onsets that lstm_wqa warns and the forecast model misses, 46 (36%) are missed even when the slots hold the perfect rain; the difference at the fixed level sits in onsets with little rain on the target day (220 of 611 with under 5 mm: 80% warned without the forecast, 42% with it, 62% with the perfect rain in the slots), follows the seasons (points of onsets warned, forecast model minus lstm_wqa: DJF +4.1, MAM -10.6, JJA -21.5, SON -8.9) and is found in 8 of 12 basins; and the forecast is light where the onsets are (it carries 0.69 of the AORC rain on the onset days and 0.63 on those with at least 5 mm, a conditional bias that the single bias factor does not remove) and has 36% exact zeros against 51% in the AORC rain. No experiment here isolates the cause: the alternatives are the warning level, small-rain onsets and a conditional bias of the forecast. Forward passes of the saved networks (forward_pass_tests; information only, nothing retrained): slots = (1 - w) x the perfect rain + w x the forecast, onsets warned at 1 day for w = 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1: 69.1%, 64.6%, 58.6%, 51.2%, 44.5%; the first quarter of the way from the perfect rain to the forecast costs 18%/19%/19% of the drop in onsets warned at 1/2/3 days (a linear response would cost 25%), so the response is gradual, not steep at small departures from exact slots, which a reliance on exactness would predict; the forecast values below 0.5 mm set to zero: 44.2%, below 1 mm: 43.9% (at most 0.7 points of difference from the forecast at any lead).

The control and the perfect-rain set are therefore 'the same network with another input' up to the stopping update: the control measures what a network that trusts its slots does when they hold no information, and wqaP what it does when they are right.

More seeds where the NSE decides: the median NSE of the single trainings of a set spans up to 0.077 (lead 1, lstm_wqa_s); with three seeds the NSE rule of report section 4.2 can hardly ever call a gain of a few hundredths clear. The onsets warned, pooled over the basins, are decided by the seeds more easily.
The simple-model yardstick was run on the main split only (the substitution design); ridge regression and the random forest were not retrained on the satellite-era split with the forecast.
A forecast issued later than the 00 UTC run (00:30 local, the 06 UTC run) was not tried; the Eastern-summer margin of the rule is slightly negative (see the notes).

Training with a mixture of AORC and forecast rain in the slots (or noise on the AORC rain), which could narrow the gap between the substitution and the retrained model, was not tried; the settings of the LSTM (hidden size, learning rate, dropout, budget) were not tuned for the forecast sets.

No seasonal bias correction (one factor per basin and lead), no spatial detail finer than the 0.25 degree boxes, no lead other than 1 to 3 days, no leave-one-basin-out test, no peaks-and-onsets loss (E5), no change of the network (E6).
The real-time products that would replace AORC in the 'rain to midnight' column (Stage IV, MRMS) were not used here: the base rung inherits E1b's caveats about AORC.

The tests of the over-trust reading that need more than forward passes: synthetic slots with the forecast's measured conditional bias but no random error (and the reverse), a retraining of wqaF_sub with a mixture or noise in the training slots, and a control with constant slots (the monthly climatology of the rain) were not run; until they are, the over-trust sentence stays a hypothesis.

A seasonal or quantile-mapped bias correction fitted on 2000-2005 (the single factor per basin and lead is noisy and leaves a seasonal and a conditional bias) was not tried, and neither was a check of the reforecast's skill against a few months of operational GEFS before any real-time claim.
